guide.title: New to padel? Start here.
guide.intro: Padel is doubles tennis on a smaller court, surrounded by glass walls you can play off. Most people rally within ten minutes of their first game. Here's what you need to know before booking.
guide.courtIntro: A padel court is 20 × 10 metres, enclosed by glass back walls and mesh side fencing. The ball stays in play after bouncing off a wall, as long as it bounced on the ground first.
guide.rulesTitle: Five rules for your first game

rules.title: Always doubles
rules.body: Courts are built for four players. Split the court price four ways and you have the per-player cost shown on every club card.

rules.title: Serve underarm
rules.body: Bounce the ball behind the service line and hit it below waist height, diagonally into the opposite service box.

rules.title: Ground first, then walls
rules.body: The ball must bounce once on your side before it touches a wall. After that, you can let it rebound off the glass and play it.

rules.title: Tennis scoring
rules.body: Points go 15, 30, 40, game. Six games win a set, and most friendly matches are best of three sets or whatever fits your booking.

rules.title: Mind the side fences
rules.body: Balls that hit the mesh fencing bounce unpredictably. Beginners should aim through the middle of the court.

kit: Court or clay-court trainers with a herringbone sole
A racket. Most clubs hire them for a few euros
A tube of padel balls, which are slightly softer than tennis balls
Water and a towel, especially for outdoor summer slots

levels.name: Starter
levels.description: First few games. You're learning the serve and getting used to the walls.

levels.name: Improver
levels.description: You can rally, and you're starting to use the back glass on purpose.

levels.name: Intermediate
levels.description: Consistent volleys, lobs, and the bandeja. You'll enjoy league nights.

levels.name: Advanced
levels.description: Competitive play, smashes off the wall, and tournament entries.

faqs.question: How long should I book?
faqs.answer: Ninety minutes is the standard slot at every club listed here. It's long enough to warm up and play two sets.

faqs.question: Do I need a partner to book?
faqs.answer: You book the whole court, so it's easiest with three friends. Many clubs run social mix-ins or can pair you with other players. Ask when you call.

faqs.question: Indoor, covered, or outdoor?
faqs.answer: Indoor halls are playable in any weather. Covered courts keep the rain off but stay open to the breeze. Outdoor courts are cheapest and best on mild evenings.

faqs.question: What is a bandeja?
faqs.answer: It's padel's signature overhead: a controlled, sliced shot that keeps you at the net. It's also where this directory gets its name.

guide.ctaBody: Pick a club near you and give them a call. Off-peak weekday mornings are the easiest slots to get.
